newsitem.title: CHINA: China raises $1.4 billion in foreign bonds in '96.
newsitem.headline: China raises $1.4 billion in foreign bonds in '96.

text.p: China's Ministry of Finance raised $1.4 billion in bond issues in the world's capital markets in 1996, the China Securities newspaper said on Saturday.
Since China re-entered the world capital markets in 1993, it has raised a total of $4 billion in seven bond issues, the newspaper said.
The 1996 issue included $400 million in Yankee bonds, with $300 million having a seven-year term and $100 million having a 100-year term, it said.
The remaining $1 billion were global bonds, with $700 million for five years and $300 million for 10 years, it said.
The successful issue of these bonds showed the confidence of international investors in China's economic development and helped to develop the European and American debt markets, the newspaper said.

But the government continues to rely mainly on domestic debt to finance the country's construction, with a total bond issue in 1996 of more than 190 billion yuan, of which domestic bonds accounted for 180 billion yuan and foreign bonds more than 10 billion yuan, it said but gave no more details. ($1 = 8.3 yuan)
